title: Sections of a limit with epimorphic transitions
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $(F_n)_{n\geq1}$ an inverse system of abelian sheaves on
$X_{\Proet}$ with epimorphic transition maps, and $F=\varprojlim_nF_n$. Then the
canonical map $F\to R\varprojlim_nF_n$ is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\Proet})$, and
for every object $W$ of $X_{\Proet}$

$$
R\Gamma(W,F)\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)
$$

in $D(\mathbf Z)$; here $R\varprojlim$ of a sequence $(K_n)$ is the fibre of
$1-\text{shift}\colon\prod_nK_n\to\prod_nK_n$.

proof.text: Regard each abelian sheaf $F_n$, with its transition maps, as a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf Z_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; a $\mathbf Z_X$-module structure on an abelian sheaf exists and is unique, so abelian sheaves and $\mathbf Z_X$-modules are the same category and $D(X_{\Proet})=D(X_{\Proet},\mathbf Z_X)$. Reindex the tower by $m=n-1\geq0$. By [det-pe-products-derived], the termwise product $P=\prod_nF_n$ with its coordinate projections is a product of the $F_n$ in $D(X_{\Proet})$, and $1-T$ on $P$ (with $T$ the transition endomorphism of [det-pe-milnor-sequence]) is $1-\text{shift}$ on that product. Hence a fibre of $1-\text{shift}$ in the sense of the statement is $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$, the convention $R\varprojlim_nF_n$ of [det-pe-milnor-sequence], together with its rotated cone triangle $R\varprojlim_nF_n\to P\xrightarrow{1-T}P\to R\varprojlim_nF_n[1]$, distinguished by the cone convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The epimorphic-tower comparison [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic], applied with $\mathcal R=\mathbf Z_X$ to this module tower, says that the canonical map $(\varprojlim_nF_n)[0]\to R\varprojlim_nF_n$ is an isomorphism. Since the stated $F$ is the ordinary inverse limit $\varprojlim_nF_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], this proves the first assertion.

source.place: first paragraph: replete-topos comparison $R\varprojlim_nF_n\simeq\varprojlim_nF_n$ for epimorphic towers, with the product $\prod_nF_n$ computing the derived product (Bhatt-Scholze, Propositions 3.1.9 and 3.1.10)

proof.text: Compose the triangle of step 1 with the isomorphism $F[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_nF_n$ of step 1. This gives a distinguished triangle $F\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-T}P\xrightarrow{\delta}F[1]$ in $D(X_{\Proet},\mathbf Z_X)$, where $P$ is a product of the $F_n$ in this triangulated category by [det-pe-products-derived] and $p$ has coordinates the limit projections. By [def-weil-derived-limit] this is a Roos triangle: $(F,p,\delta)$ is a derived limit of the tower $(F_n)$ (the sign convention for $\delta$ is immaterial, as recorded there). Now apply [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] with the small site $X_{\Proet}$ (small in a larger universe), the sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O=\mathbf Z_X$, the object $U=W$ and $K_n=F_n[0]$. Its $R\Gamma(W,-)$ is computed from K-injective resolutions of $\mathbf Z_X$-modules, which, for sheaves in degree $0$, is the derived sections functor of the statement. The lemma says that the maps $R\Gamma(W,\operatorname{pr}_n)$ identify $R\Gamma(W,P)$ with $\prod_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)$ in $D(\mathbf Z)$. They also turn the image of the triangle into a derived-limit triangle for the tower $(R\Gamma(W,F_n),R\Gamma(W,t_n))$, whose middle map is $1-\text{shift}$ on $\prod_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)$. Hence $R\Gamma(W,F)$ is a fibre of $1-\text{shift}\colon\prod_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)\to\prod_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)$, that is, $R\Gamma(W,F)\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)$ in $D(\mathbf Z)$ with the meaning fixed in the statement.

source.place: second paragraph: 'The functor $R\Gamma(W,-)$ ... is triangulated and, as a right adjoint, preserves products. Applying it to the triangle ... gives the triangle defining $R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)$'

split_report.summary: Audited the imported two-paragraph proof. Step 1: abelian sheaves are Z_X-modules; det-pe-products-derived makes the termwise product the product in D(X_proet), so the statement's fibre of 1-shift is the Cone(1-T)[-1] of det-pe-milnor-sequence, and det-pe-milnor-epimorphic gives F[0] = R lim F_n (Bhatt-Scholze 3.1.9-3.1.10). Step 2: the resulting triangle is a Roos triangle (def-weil-derived-limit), and the site-general lemma lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit applied to O=Z_X, U=W gives R Gamma(W,F) = R lim R Gamma(W,F_n). (Maintainer reader repair: step 2 originally took R Gamma(W,-) to be a right adjoint, which no cited node states, and used the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits. It also omitted the identification of the termwise product with the derived product.) No statement change, no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the first paragraph of det-pe-continuous-cohomology-limit.proof.md (repleteness via det-pe-milnor-epimorphic, derived product via det-pe-products-derived); step 2 realizes the second paragraph (R Gamma(W,-) applied to the Roos triangle), with the blueprint's 'as a right adjoint, preserves products' carried by lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit.

tool_uses.why: Step 2 takes from its statement, as a black box, that R Gamma(U,-) on module sheaves of a small site identifies R Gamma(U, prod K_n) with prod R Gamma(U,K_n) and sends Roos triangles to Roos triangles. This is the 'right adjoint preserves products' sentence of the blueprint proof. No node of sk-prop-pe-continuous-cohomology or of the units it cites states the commutation of derived sections with products or derived limits.
